claim: All property subject to taxation must be assessed at 35 percent of its taxable value.
Appeals to the county board of equalization must be filed not later than January 15 (next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday).
An appeal under NRS 361.357 (full cash value less than taxable value) cannot result in an increase in taxable value.
A taxpayer aggrieved by the county board may appeal to the State Board of Equalization on or before March 10.
Before filing a county board appeal, the owner must complete a form provided by the county assessor.
UNCONFIRMED: Whether the 35% assessment ratio is applied to a 'taxable value' computed by cost approach less depreciation (not confirmed on opened pages).
The Nevada homestead exemption extends only to equity not exceeding $605,000 unless allodial title is established.
A declaration of homestead must be signed, acknowledged and recorded like conveyances of real property.
A homestead is not deemed abandoned without a written declaration signed and acknowledged by both spouses or the single claimant, and recorded.
Exemption is protection from execution/creditors, not a property tax exemption.
cite: NRS 115.010 heading (exemption from sale on execution)

claim: UNCONFIRMED: No state property-tax homestead exemption was located; Nevada senior/veteran/disabled property tax exemptions and tax-credit programs were not researched.
Base RPTT is $1.95 per $500 of value or fraction thereof where value exceeds $100.
Washoe and Churchill counties add $0.10 and Clark County adds $0.60 to the base rate.
NRS 375.020 imposes 65 cents per $500 in counties under 700,000 population and NRS 375.023 adds $1.30 per $500.
Buyer and seller are jointly and severally liable for the tax; the escrow holder is not liable.
Each deed presented for recording must be accompanied by a declaration of value.
Exemptions include transfers between former spouses under a divorce decree, transfers to relatives within the first degree of lineal consanguinity or affinity, and deeds upon death.
The tax is collected by the county recorder when the deed is recorded.
UNCONFIRMED: Exact current county-by-county rate for counties other than Clark, Washoe, Churchill beyond the $1.95 base.
Nevada deeds of trust are generally foreclosed nonjudicially by the trustee's power of sale; a notice of breach and election to sell must be recorded in each county where the property lies.
The grantor or title holder has 35 days (for deeds after July 1, 1957) to cure after the notice is recorded and mailed.
Not less than 3 months must elapse after recording the notice of default before sale.
Notice of sale must be posted for 20 days and published once a week for 3 consecutive weeks in a county newspaper.
Sale is at public auction to the highest bidder between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m.
A sale vests title in the purchaser without equity or right of redemption.
For owner-occupied housing, notice 'Your home loan is being foreclosed' must be served not later than 60 days before the sale.
Deficiency application must be made within 6 months after the foreclosure sale; financial institutions cannot obtain one for qualifying purchase-money owner-occupied single-family homes.
UNCONFIRMED: Foreclosure Mediation Program details (not opened).
Execution sale notice must be published three times, once a week for 3 successive weeks, in a newspaper if one exists in the county.
Sales under execution are made at auction to the highest bidder.
The judgment debtor or redemptioner may redeem within 1 year after the sale by paying the purchase price plus 1 percent per month.
If not redeemed within 1 year, the purchaser is entitled to a conveyance (sheriff's deed).
The sheriff's certificate of sale must state if the sale is subject to redemption.
UNCONFIRMED: Posting period (20 days) on execution notices not directly seen.
A small estate affidavit may be used 40 days after death without letters of administration if the decedent left no real property or interest therein in Nevada.
The applicable amount is $150,000 for a surviving spouse claimant and $25,000 for any other claimant.
A procedure exists to set aside estates not exceeding $150,000 by court petition.
Real property may pass by deed upon death recorded before the owner's death, then a Death of Grantor Affidavit with death certificate and declaration of value is recorded.
UNCONFIRMED: Process for selling inherited real property through formal probate/independent administration (NRS 148) not opened.
NRS 375A.100 imposes a tax on transfer of a taxable estate equal to the maximum credit allowable against the federal estate tax for state death taxes.
Nevada economic development office states Nevada has no corporate income tax, personal income tax, inheritance/gift tax, or estate tax.
UNCONFIRMED: Whether the federal credit currently results in zero Nevada estate tax (inference not confirmed on an opened official page).
County recorders record documents authorized or required by law to be recorded, and may deny recording within 2 judicial days if unlawful.
Recording fee is $25 for recording a document, plus statutory additional fees ($7 under NRS 247.305(3), up to $5 and up to $6 county-authorized).
Names of all signers must be typed or printed beneath original signatures.
Recording is in the county recorder's office of the county where the property is located; deeds need a declaration of value.
UNCONFIRMED: E-recording availability and APN/mailing address requirements (NRS 111.312) not confirmed beyond the section title; county-specific fees may differ.
No estate in land is created except by operation of law or written conveyance.
Quitclaim transfers are still subject to RPTT unless exempt (e.g., first-degree relatives, divorce decree).
A deed transferring title for nominal consideration is valued at estimated fair market value for RPTT.
UNCONFIRMED: Statutory quitclaim form language and effect (not found on official pages opened).
Property taxes are a perpetual lien until paid, superior to all other liens and encumbrances.
The lien attaches July 1 of the year for which taxes are levied.
The county treasurer mails notice of delinquency before issuing a certificate to the treasurer as trustee.
UNCONFIRMED: Penalty and interest rates on delinquent taxes.
After delinquency, the county treasurer is issued a certificate to hold the property as trustee, subject to redemption within 2 years (1 year if abandoned).
A deed to the county treasurer as trustee issues after the period of redemption.
UNCONFIRMED: Whether Nevada conducts a tax-lien-certificate auction versus trustee deed sale details; amounts to redeem.
Summary eviction for nonpayment is under NRS 40.253; other bases under NRS 40.254.
Tenant may contest by filing an affidavit before close of business on the fifth judicial day after service of notice.
Landlord applies by affidavit to justice court or district court; the court holds a hearing once the tenant files the affidavit.
The court may issue a summary order for removal; sheriff or constable posts it within 24 hours of receipt.
UNCONFIRMED: Length of the notice period for nonpayment under current law (statute text opened was fragmentary).
On voluntary sale, the new owner has the previous owner's rights and obligations under the existing rental agreement unless modified.
New owner must notify the tenant within 30 days of transfer with contact information and security deposit amount.
Before recording a deed, the landlord must transfer remaining security deposits to the successor in writing or notify that deposits were returned.
Successor must accept the existing deposit and may not require an additional deposit during the term.
UNCONFIRMED: Exact section number for the 30-day new owner notice.
In Nevada the seller usually pays for the owner's title policy and the buyer for the lender's policy, negotiable.

claim: RPTT is jointly and severally owed by buyer and seller.
UNCONFIRMED: Whether an attorney is required (Nevada is generally escrow/title company practice; not confirmed on opened page).
Nevada has no personal income tax, so no state tax on capital gains.
UNCONFIRMED: Confirmation from tax.nv.gov that there is no personal income tax; federal capital gains rules are outside scope.
A land sale installment contract is one where the seller retains title until full price is paid, then transfers by written instrument.
RPTT applies to land sale installment contracts exceeding $100 in value.
Sellers must record the contract within 30 calendar days after first payment and pay the chapter 375 tax.
UNCONFIRMED: Other chapter 598 protections for land sale installment contracts.
At least 10 days before conveyance, the seller must complete a disclosure form and serve the purchaser or agent.
A seller's agent shall not complete the disclosure form for the seller.
If a seller fails to serve the form, the purchaser may rescind before conveyance without penalty.
Rescission is effective only if in writing, notarized and served within 4 working days after the purchaser is informed of the defect.
A seller who conveys without disclosing known defects may be liable for treble repair cost plus fees; action within 1 year of discovery or 2 years after conveyance, whichever is later.
The form does not constitute a warranty; unknown defects need not be disclosed.
Real Estate Division Form 547 is the Seller's Real Property Disclosure Form.
UNCONFIRMED: Exemptions for trustees/beneficiaries in foreclosure sales detailed in NRS 113.130(2).
The court shall, to the extent practicable, make an equal disposition of community property, unequal only for a compelling reason set out in writing.
Transfer of title between former spouses under a divorce decree is exempt from RPTT.
UNCONFIRMED: Residency requirement and treatment of separate property.
Seller must serve the disclosure form at least 10 days before conveyance in FSBO sales too.
RPTT is collected at recording and declaration of value must accompany the deed.
Seller transferring a tenant-occupied unit must transfer security deposits before recording.
UNCONFIRMED: Whether owners are exempt from real estate licensing in NRS 645 (not opened).
Deficiency judgment limited to the lesser of debt minus fair market value or debt minus sale price (principal residence, one structure up to four families).
A financial institution cannot get a deficiency on qualifying owner-occupied purchase-money single-family foreclosure.
A seller must still disclose known defects even when selling as-is.
UNCONFIRMED: Short-sale-specific deficiency waiver statute (NRS 40.4639) not confirmed.
An owner may create a deed upon death conveying property to beneficiaries effective on the owner's death.
It is valid only if executed and recorded with the county recorder before the owner's death.
Capacity required is the same as to make a will.
It is effective without notice to or consideration from the beneficiary.
If multiple deeds are recorded, the last recorded before death is effective.
After death, a Death of Grantor Affidavit with declaration of value and death certificate must be recorded.
Transfers by deed upon death are exempt from RPTT.
